summary: U.S. markets extended losses into a third consecutive session as Treasury yields surged to multi-decade highs, with the 30-year bond yield reaching its highest level since 2007 at approximately 5.32%. The S&P 500 fell 0.69% to 7,691.76 on Tuesday while the Nasdaq dropped 1.33% to 26,289.71, weighed down by a sharp semiconductor selloff that intensified globally. Asian markets tumbled overnight with South Korea's Kospi plunging 5.5% as chip giants Samsung and SK Hynix each shed over 7%. Retail earnings from Target and Lowe's hit premarket screens Wednesday morning alongside semiconductor results from Analog Devices. Crypto markets showed modest gains with Bitcoin opening Tuesday up 2.7% to $64,487 and Ethereum rising 2% to $1,911, though both remain mired in an extended bear market amid geopolitical uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict. The bond rout reflects persistent inflation concerns and elevated oil prices, raising questions about the Fed's ability to hold rates steady at the September meeting despite Chair Warsh's dovish July stance.

signals.title: 30-year Treasury yield hits 19-year high as global bond selloff intensifies
signals.desc: The U.S. 30-year bond yield scored a fresh 19-year high while Japan's 10-year reached a 30-year peak, tightening financial conditions and pressuring equity valuations across growth stocks.

signals.title: Semiconductor stocks plunge globally as Asia selloff deepens
signals.desc: Samsung and SK Hynix fell over 7% while Western Digital dropped 7% and Marvell declined 8%, signaling a broad retreat from the year's hottest AI-chip trade amid valuation concerns.

signals.title: Major retailers Target and Lowe's report Q2 earnings Wednesday morning
signals.desc: Results will provide critical datapoints on consumer health as elevated bond yields and Middle East uncertainty weigh on discretionary spending outlooks.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum post modest Tuesday gains despite extended bear market
signals.desc: BTC opened up 2.7% to $64,487 and ETH rose 2% to $1,911, but analysts remain split on whether the bottom is near as both cryptos remain down since the Iran conflict began in late February.

signals.title: Fed dissent signals hawkish pressure as inflation concerns persist
signals.desc: Three FOMC members dissented at the July meeting wanting to hike rates, reflecting division as Chair Warsh holds the line at 3.5%-3.75% amid sticky inflation and elevated oil prices.

verdict: Risk-off sentiment persists as bond yields pressure equities; retail earnings and semiconductor weakness will dictate whether Tuesday's decline extends into a broader correction.
